method.summary: How long does one keyless documentation call to this server take, from a caller that is nobody in particular? Fifteen calls to `hf_fs` with the operation `search hf://docs QUERY`: five plain-language questions inside the scope the tool's own description claims, each sent three times in three rounds. Median 361.0 ms, min 305.3, max 1077.4, IQR 384.2; round medians 826.3, 335.2, 313.9 ms; 0 failures. DEVIATION, NAMED: this solution was first recorded INELIGIBLE in the 12:31Z run on a misreading of its own tool description - the full `hf_fs` text lists `hf://docs` among its search scopes and says documentation search requires a QUERY - so its fifteen calls were taken at 12:53Z, about twenty minutes after the other eight, and were NOT round-robin with them. They did not get the protection the protocol's interleaving exists to give, which makes them less comparable to the other eight than those are to each other. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a server-side latency. Every number includes this container, its HTTP proxy and one day's public internet from a single vantage point. Response size is not controlled and is published beside every duration (median 2909 bytes of text). The round medians show the clearest cold start in the run: 826.3 ms falling to 313.9 ms. NO BASELINE, deliberately: 'within the agent's turn' is not a number, and inventing one so the coverage table resolved would be filling a cell to make the map look finished. NO RANKING and no comparison with the other records from this run.
method.dataset: Five questions, each sent three times: How do I load a LoRA adapter with PEFT?; How do I stream a dataset with the datasets library?; How do I push a model to the Hub from code?; How do I run text generation with a pipeline in Transformers?; How do I quantize a model with bitsandbytes?
